issues.issue: Did the judge breach natural justice through bias or by failing to hear the appellant on common-law immunity?
issues.applicant_position: Judge's reasons show surprising bias, and he failed to recognize a right to hear the common-law immunity question.
issues.respondent_position: No bias is shown in the reasons; the judge drew no conclusion on common-law immunity, so no breach occurred.
issues.result_quote: Consequently, the judge did not breach the audi alterem partem rule in any way, as the appellant submits.

issues.issue: Is the IRB bound to pay the appellant's defence costs for criminal charges arising from his IAD duties, on judicial-independence grounds?
issues.applicant_position: As an IAD member with judge-like powers, judicial independence requires the IRB to pay his defence costs.
issues.respondent_position: not stated; the IRB refused payment under the Treasury Board indemnification policy and the Legal Assistance Policy.
issues.result_quote: I am unable to conclude that a superior court judge facing charges similar to those laid against the appellant, could demand that the Crown pay his legal costs and fees.

issues.issue: Can the appellant invoke judicial immunity against the criminal charges?
issues.applicant_position: Does not contend he is immune from the criminal prosecution itself (para 43).
issues.result_quote: It is clear from these authorities that the appellant is unable to invoke judicial immunity from the charges now weighing against him.

issues.issue: Does an IAD member have the same powers, rights and privileges as a superior court judge?
issues.applicant_position: Says an IAD member has the same powers as a superior court judge; the Court assumes this for argument only.
issues.result_quote: it is unnecessary for us to decide whether the appellant, in his capacity as a member of the Immigration Appeal Division of the IRB, has powers
